scope: Recipe-5 Bézier editing in the local authoring prototype; no game install or runtime claim

contract.legacy: v1–v4 remain Catmull–Rom with unchanged masks; conversion is explicit and undoable
contract.split: de Casteljau subdivision preserves the continuous cubic and parameter-linear pigment targets

browser.isolation: verification browser draft and SQLite database only

numericObservations.note: Analytic curve conversion/split preservation does not imply identical finite polygon raster samples. Historical recipes do not automatically convert.

limitations: Extreme legal ±1 UV handles produced 2410/9644 segments for 6/24 knots. Measured 32-square rasters cost 36.6/116.1 ms; full-atlas 1024 estimates of 37.5/118.9 seconds are extrapolations, not measured runs.
Queued raster jobs coalesce per layer and stale results are discarded, but running jobs cannot yet be cancelled; worker-error recovery also needs improvement.
Surface guide construction scans mesh triangles for each curve segment on the main thread. Worker cancellation alone cannot guarantee fluid extreme-curve editing.
Collapsed UV tangent proxies become actual endpoints after nonzero movement; geometry remains continuous but the diamond can visually approach the knot.
Off-plate handles use the UV editor rather than fabricated face anchors.
Glitter correction, directional softness, whole-shape transforms and UV pan/zoom remain separate queued work.
provenance: Project-authored curve mathematics and adapters; existing Three.js/Bun/SQLite dependency credits extended. No new community code or artwork copied.
